about: Hand-written expectations for the intended changes from the TypeScript SQLite adapter (src/lib/db/sqlite.ts); see 'Task 8' in docs/plans/2026-09-26-rust-core-phase-2-plan.md. The recorder never writes this file; its 'scratch' block is what record mode (in a fresh temp-file database) and tests/smoke.rs build. Fix 1: table names are bound (pragma_table_info(?), pragma_index_list(?), pragma_foreign_key_list(?)) or quoted with " doubled (row counts) instead of passed through validateIdentifier, which rejected any name with a space, '-' or a quote, so such tables showed no columns, indexes or row count ('columns'/'indexes' cases, checked live). Fix 2: the DDL quote doubles ". Fix 3: an added index is CREATE INDEX "schema"."name" ON "table" (SQLite rejects a schema-qualified table there). Fix 4: SQLite has no ALTER TABLE ... ADD FOREIGN KEY, so a foreign key on an existing column is a comment line saying the table must be recreated; one on a column added in the same edit (without a default, as SQLite requires) goes inline: ADD COLUMN c ... REFERENCES "t" ("id"). Fix 5: index columns come from pragma_index_info (the TS listed none); an expression key is '<expression>'. Fix 6: with no ALTER COLUMN in SQLite, a type, nullability or default edit was dropped silently (the TS returned '-- No changes detected'); it is now a comment line naming the column and what changed. No table-rebuild recipe (follow-up). Comment lines follow every statement, so a client that splits on ';\n' and skips '--' lines still runs every statement; line breaks in names become spaces so nothing escapes the comment. Fix 7: the autoindexes behind UNIQUE and PRIMARY KEY constraints (sqlite_autoindex_*) are listed, marked unique, and counted in the statistics; since the table editor copies them into its definition, removing one there is a comment line (SQLite can't drop them) instead of DROP INDEX. Fix 8: EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN details the TS regexes missed: names that aren't one ASCII word, numbered subqueries (SCALAR/LIST SUBQUERY n), SCAN CONSTANT ROW, BLOOM FILTER, LEFT-JOIN/RIGHT-JOIN, virtual tables, LAST n TERMS OF ORDER BY, count(DISTINCT), a bare SEARCH (rowid seek). Fix 9 (found while recording): a foreign key declared without parent columns (REFERENCES customers) has a NULL 'to'; the TS showed referencedColumn null, the fixed query resolves it to the parent's primary key column at the same position. Its 'replaces' case only records the parser side: the TS query's NULL 'to' reads as "" because the reference column is a String on the wire. Fix 10 (found while recording): NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%' treats '_' as a wildcard, so the TS hid user tables such as 'sqlitex' from the schema and statistics; only the reserved 'sqlite_' prefix is hidden now. A case with 'replaces' supersedes the recorded case of that name (the parity tests assert the recorded TypeScript output differs); its 'input' is null: the recorded case's input applies. Fix 11 (Task 10): SQLite has no DEFAULT in UPDATE, so Set to default was a syntax error; given the column's default expression from its metadata (defaultValue, the text of pragma_table_info's dflt_value, or NULL for a column without one), the dialect assigns it in parentheses: SET "c" = (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP). A bare-word or quoted-name default (DEFAULT active, DEFAULT "dq", `bt`, [br]) is stored as a string by SQLite but would read a column as an expression, so it becomes a string literal; numbers (+1, -0x10), blob literals, keywords and (expr) defaults stay as they are. 'crud-set-default' cases are checked by tests/dialect_parity.rs and executed by tests/smoke.rs; without a columnDefault the TypeScript statement is kept.

setup: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT UNIQUE, status TEXT DEFAULT 'active', score REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, note TEXT)
CREATE INDEX customers_name_idx ON customers (name)
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX customers_status_email_idx ON customers (status, email)
CREATE INDEX customers_lower_email_idx ON customers (lower(email), id)
CREATE INDEX customers_vip_idx ON customers (note) WHERE note = 'vip'

INSERT INTO customers (name, email, score, note) WITH RECURSIVE seq (n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM seq WHERE n < 200) SELECT 'Customer ' || n, 'c' || n || '@example.com', n % 50, CASE WHEN n % 3 = 0 THEN 'vip' END FROM seq

CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers (id) ON DELETE CASCADE, kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('click', 'view', 'buy')), total NUMERIC(10,2), placed_at TEXT NOT NULL, memo BLOB)
CREATE INDEX orders_customer_kind_idx ON orders (customer_id, kind)

INSERT INTO orders (customer_id, kind, total, placed_at, memo) WITH RECURSIVE seq (n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM seq WHERE n < 1000) SELECT n % 200 + 1, CASE n % 3 WHEN 0 THEN 'click' WHEN 1 THEN 'view' ELSE 'buy' END, n % 97, datetime('2026-01-01', '+' || n || ' minutes'), CASE WHEN n % 10 = 0 THEN X'00ff' END FROM seq
CREATE TABLE accounts (customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers, region TEXT NOT NULL, balance REAL, PRIMARY KEY (customer_id, region))
CREATE TABLE kv (k TEXT PRIMARY KEY, v) WITHOUT ROWID
CREATE TABLE "order items" (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, "order id" INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES orders (id), sku TEXT NOT NULL, qty INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, UNIQUE ("order id", sku))
CREATE INDEX "order items sku idx" ON "order items" (sku)
CREATE TABLE "my-table" (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT DEFAULT 'n/a')
CREATE TABLE "it's" (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, "say ""hi""" TEXT)
CREATE TABLE "café" ("naïve" TEXT DEFAULT 'é', v INTEGER)
CREATE INDEX "café_naïve_idx" ON "café" ("naïve")

CREATE TABLE ledger (account_id INTEGER, account_region TEXT, amount REAL, FOREIGN KEY (account_id, account_region) REFERENCES accounts (customer_id, region), FOREIGN KEY (account_id, account_region) REFERENCES accounts)
CREATE TABLE sqlitex (id INTEGER)
CREATE TABLE a (x INTEGER, y INTEGER)
CREATE TABLE b (x INTEGER, y INTEGER)
INSERT INTO a VALUES (1,1),(2,2),(3,3)
INSERT INTO b VALUES (2,2),(3,3),(4,4)
CREATE VIEW customer_names AS SELECT id, name FROM customers
ANALYZE
